articles.title: Projeto Paradiso Founder Olga Rabinovich to Receive Inaugural Encounters Award at the São Paulo Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Philanthropist Olga Rabinovich will receive the inaugural Prêmio Encontros (Encounters Award) at this year’s Encontro de Ideias Audiovisuais, the industry platform of the São Paulo International Film Festival.
body: Philanthropist Olga Rabinovich will receive the inaugural Prêmio Encontros (Encounters Award) at this year’s Encontro de Ideias Audiovisuais, the industry platform of the São Paulo International Film Festival. The award honors her enduring commitment to advancing Brazilian cinema and elevating the international profile of Brazilian film and talent through her work with Projeto Paradiso.

“Olga Rabinovich is the first recipient of the newly created Prêmio Encontros, because she was the inspiration behind the award,” said Renata de Almeida, director of the São Paulo International Film Festival. I first heard Olga’s name in early 2018, when Josephine Bourgois came to see me about someone from the private sector who wanted to create an institute dedicated to cinema. The Olga Rabinovich Institute was announced during the 42nd Mostra, bringing a breath of hope at a time that promised to be particularly difficult for Brazilian film and culture.”

articles.title: Noel Gallagher guitar sells for £12,000 at auction
articles.summary: The instrument was one of a number of items which belonged to a former Oasis sound engineer.
body: A guitar which originally belonged to Noel Gallagher has been sold for £12,000 at auction.
The limited edition Epiphone instrument in Manchester City blue was one of a number of items put up for sale by the son of Huw Richards, a former front-of-house sound engineer with the band.
Another of the items in his collection, a Kangol rain jacket produced for the band's touring personnel, sold for £2,000.
But a set of unheard Oasis recordings valued at between £1.2m and £1.6m were pulled from the auction last week, after the band filed an injunction.

articles.title: Skydance Blasts Off: Can David Ellison Make Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Fly?
articles.summary: David Ellison has emerged victorious. And he’s boldly — or arrogantly, if you prefer — decided to name the entertainment giant that he’s bolted together Skydance Corp., nodding to the original name of his film production firm that has swallowed up two Hollywood studios over the past 14 months.
body: “They need to move as quickly as possible to get the leverage down,” says Jawad Hussain, managing director at S&P Global. “The biggest hurdle and the biggest thing we’re going to be keeping our eye on is integration and execution.” Two years ago, Hussain says, Skydance Meida was a small company that turned out a few films a year. “Now it’s managing one of the largest media companies. It’s not necessarily an easy task.”
It’s all been a whirlwind. On the morning of Sept. 30, Ellison still didn’t know if it was a done deal.

He had spent more than a year in his relentless pursuit of acquiring Warner Bros. and HBO. The WBD board rejected his takeover offers eight times. David Zaslav, Warner Bros. Discovery’s boss, ghosted Ellison in December 2025 after Netflix clinched a deal for WB’s streaming and studios business. But Ellison didn’t surrender; he finally outbid Netflix in February, with a $31/share offer that was nearly 2.5 times the stock price before the M&A frenzy kicked off. It was an offer WBD couldn’t refuse.

articles.title: Alison Hammond returns home from hospital after rushing off This Morning
articles.summary: The This Morning presenter said she believes she experienced a panic attack on Friday's show.
body: Alison Hammond has said she is home and "feeling so much better" after she went to hospital for a heart check-up after leaving ITV's This Morning midway through Friday's show.

The presenter, 51, left the programme during its live broadcast, appearing to clutch her chest as she was helped off set by co-host Dermot O'Leary. He later told viewers she was "feeling a little unwell".
Soon after Hammond said she had "a little bit of a palpitation" and was undergoing tests.
In a video on Instagram on Saturday, she said she was "all OK, all-clear, which would mean I had a massive panic attack on live TV. I mean, the shame of it."

articles.title: ‘April X’ Review: Connor Storrie Bides His Time in a Generic Sci-Fi Clone
articles.summary: It would be nice to say that Connor Storrie burns up the screen in “April X,” the star’s first film vehicle released since TV’s “Heated Rivalry” made him hot property, but it would be overstating the case.
body: Shot before 'Heated Rivalry' launched its leading man to stardom, Michel K. Parandi's murky futuristic thriller will only be remembered — if at all — for that fortunate casting coup.

The year is unspecified, but the fatigued brutalist housing blocks of outer Bucharest are still standing: Though it doesn’t specify a location either, “April X” uses the present-day wear and tear of the Romanian capital, where the film was shot on location, as shorthand for a world collapsing into concrete ruin. The odd hi-tech drone adds some futuristic pizzazz to the film’s exterior vistas, but the new technologies defining the narrative aren’t of the gleaming, brave-new-world variety: People are being cloned in grubby, shadowed fashion, while memories and dreams can be captured and downloaded onto surprisingly retro-looking data devices.

articles.title: Film festival celebrates British-Latino identity
articles.summary: The Latino film festival in the capital will screen 60 films from 27 countries over five days.
body: An event billed as London's only competitive Latino film festival is now under way for the first time in the capital.
Venues including the Barbican, the ICA, Ciné Lumière and BFI Stephen Street will screen 60 films from 27 countries until Tuesday.

There will also be workshops and performances with guests including Cuban dancer Carlos Acosta, a former principal at the Royal Ballet, Argentine actor Óscar Martínez, Cuban actor Jorge Perugorría and Oscar-winning Chilean screenwriter Gonzalo Maza.
The event was founded by Cuban actress Ketty Rodriguez who, when she moved to London, was struck by the lack of Latin representation in a city famous for its multiculturalism, film and history.

articles.title: Behemoth! review - Pedro Pascal classical music drama hits all the wrong notes
articles.summary: New York film festival: The actor stumbles through Tony Gilroy’s forgettable film marred by stylistic gimmicks. Tony Gilroy has built a sturdy career as the director of the Bourne films and show runner of the popular Star Wars spin-off Andor.
body: As the first feature film he has directed since 2012’s The Bourne Legacy, the classical music drama Behemoth! promised to be an intriguing return from a master of threading the needle between slick action and deeply felt drama. His new film comes with a score from nine A-list composers who have banded together and called themselves The Behemoth! Collective, a stacked cast and a womanizing central character who looks phenomenal in a tux: “ Tár for straight men”, as a friend of mine put it.

If only Pedro Pascal had an iota of Cate Blanchett’s charisma or Gilroy came close to Todd Field’s elegant braiding of genres. Our protagonist is Alex (Pascal), an inscrutable cello maestro who has moved home to Los Angeles after nearly two decades on the road. The city offers him regular, if soulless, session work scoring TV shows and movies, as well as the opportunity to be closer to his brother (Will Arnett) and mother, a respected harpist who is suffering from ill health.

articles.title: Zach Bryan Wears ‘Free Palestine’ Shirt During Concert at Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium: “Some Things Are Bigger Than Music, Fame and Public Approval”
articles.summary: The performance follows Gillette Stadium owner Kraft's prior controversy with Macklemore over his removal from Ed Sheeran's tour due to his pro-Palestinian statements.
body: Zach Bryan wore a “Free Palestine “ shirt while performing at Gillette Stadium on Friday night for his With Heaven On Tour following owner Robert Kraft defending his move to urge for Macklemore ‘s removal from Ed Sheeran ‘s tour after making pro-Palestinian remarks in earlier shows.

In photos and videos captured by fans and shared on social media, Bryan can be seen wearing a black shirt with the “Free Palestine“ wording while several of his band members also wore Palestine-branded clothing.
The country singer is having a two-night run at Kraft’s stadium, slated to close his tour on Saturday night.

Bryan’s “Free Palestine” shirt comes amid controversy surrounding Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium. Rapper Macklemore previously alleged that he was dropped from being an opener on Sheeran‘s tour after Kraft “rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.” During his opening set at MetLife Stadium, Macklemore had publicly shouted “Free Palestine” and showed footage from Gaza on the screen behind him.

articles.title: 10 Best Horror Movies With No Blood Or Gore, Ranked
articles.summary: If blood and gore gets you squeamish, here's a list of the best horror movies that avoid showing any of that gruesome stuff but are still scary as hell.
body: Legendary horror author H.P. Lovecraft once wrote that "the oldest and strongest emotion of mankind is fear, and the oldest and strongest kind of fear is fear of the unknown." Of course, fear is subjective, and some people genuinely freak out at the sight of blood and viscera gushing from helpless victims. But for many, the most unnerving horror comes in restraint, from films that are more selective and meticulous about what they show their audience.

While we have an extensive list of the best horror movies ever, covering everything from the terribly violent to the completely suggestive, we've distilled this list down to those movies that notably do away with much of the yucky red stuff. The films here achieve their terror through pure performance, atmosphere, implication, and insinuation, planting an unnerving inkling of fright and dread in audiences that something deeply horrifying could happen at any moment. These movies don't have a lick of gore, and yet the psychological violence of their scares wounds all the same.
Here are the 10 best horror movies with no blood or gore, ranked.

articles.title: Denver Film Festival Unveils Lineup and Honorees
articles.summary: Peter Farrelly's 'I Play Rocky' will open the fest while James Gray's 'Paper Tiger' will close it. In between, Denver Film will honor Carrie Coon, John Cho, Liz Sargent, Fred Hechinger, Benedetta Porcaroli, David Acord and experimental filmmaker Michael Gitlin.
body: Denver Film today unveiled the roster of movies and boldfaced name honorees that will make up the 49th edition of the Colorado capital city’s marquee film event, which is scheduled for Oct. 22-Nov. 1. In all, 129 features, documentaries and shorts will hit screens inside the Sie FilmCenter, Ellie Caulkins Opera House, MCA Denver at the Holiday Theater, and the Denver Museum of Nature & Science.

It’s worth noting that the showings of Josephine and Take Me Home are being co-presented with the Sundance Film Festival, which is heading to Denver Film Festival’s backyard in Boulder, Colorado in 2027. Also notable: Other picks include standout international films like TIFF’s People Choice Award winner La Bola Negra from Netflix, Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s All of a Sudden, and Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Minotaur which won a Grand Prix in Cannes.
